sources: Timeouts on outbound calls (stability patterns, Release It! by Michael Nygard)
Resource release on all paths: context managers and try/finally (https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html#with-statement-context-managers)
Unbounded in-process cache growth (concept: cache size bound and eviction)
Retry with exponential backoff and jitter (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/exponential-backoff-and-jitter/)

defects.class: missing timeout on outbound HTTP call
defects.description: Line 46 `status, body = http_get(url)` calls http_get without a timeout argument, so the client wrapper default (None) applies and the call has no deadline. Failing input: a source host accepts the TCP connection and never sends a response. fetch_source_rows blocks indefinitely, the worker thread is never returned to the pool, and after enough such feeds the pool is exhausted. fetch_with_retry in the same file passes timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, which violates R1.

Line 45 `cursor.execute(query, params)` runs after the file handle (line 43) and the cursor (line 44) are opened, and both are closed only at lines 51-52 with no finally or with block. Failing input: the query raises (for example an OperationalError on statement timeout). export_rows propagates the exception with handle and cursor still open. Repeated failing exports exhaust file descriptors and DB connections. The same leak occurs if writer.writerow raises (line 48-49). Violates R2.

defects.class: cache stampede and unbounded cache growth
defects.description: Line 45 `rows = compute_rows(key)` runs on every miss with no single-flight guard, so N concurrent requests for the same expired key execute N expensive computations. All entries stored in one burst also expire together after REPORT_TTL_SECONDS, so the stampede recurs in lockstep. Second facet: line 46 `store_report(key, rows, now)` inserts a new entry keyed by the normalised user-supplied filter text with no maximum size or eviction. Failing input: 1,000,000 distinct filter strings within 300 s create 1,000,000 entries and grow memory without bound. Violates R4 and R5 intent (R5 is about enqueue timeouts; the size bound is part of the caching requirement).

decoys.why_not_a_defect: jobs.put with timeout_seconds is a bounded blocking put. queue.Full is caught and the job is rejected with a warning, so the producer cannot block longer than ENQUEUE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (R5).
load_manifest opens the file in a with block, so the handle is closed on every path including json decode errors. Correct use of a context manager (sibling of the leaking export_rows).
run_job catches Exception, logs with exc_info via LOG.exception and re-raises JobError with `from exc`, preserving the cause chain. Broad except is intentional here and does not swallow errors.
fetch_with_retry passes timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (5.0 s) to http_get, satisfying R1. Only fetch_source_rows (line 46) omits the timeout.
peek_report deletes an expired entry under the lock and returns None, so an expired value is never served. The strict `<=` comparison is correct for a TTL boundary.
normalise_filter collapses whitespace and lowercases the key before lookup, so equivalent filters share one cache entry. Correct normalisation.

Unchanged in base and code. time.sleep(RETRY_BASE_SECONDS) is a fixed 2 s backoff with no jitter, so workers that fail together retry together. This is a real flaw against R3, but it is on an unchanged line and the change does not touch it. Diff-mode reviewers must not report it; list only here.

accepted_extras.note: open(..., 'w') truncates the output file before the query runs
